key_insight: The CALPHAD-based Gamma metric correlates better with tensile ductility in refractory compositionally complex alloys than the DFT-based D-parameter, while performing equally well in compression.
engineering_relevance: Gamma could help screen refractory alloys for room-temperature ductility, a key barrier to deploying these materials in extreme environments.
method: Compare existing ductility metrics against compressive and tensile plasticity.
Construct Gamma from BCC–HCP free-energy differences, BCC (110) surface interfacial free energy, and electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion.
Propose combining Gamma with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility to capture intrinsic and extrinsic ductility effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports modestly improved correlation with tensile ductility relative to the D-parameter but provides no dataset sizes or quantitative correlation values.
watch_item: Gamma alone does not capture oxygen-related embrittlement; the proposed oxygen-solubility extension requires validation.
paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
